messages.author: 3bd94f65c4684bac
messages.subject: Re: Just want to understand
parts:
With Weka you will have to do a lot of data preparation outside of the
tool. Although you can probably do some things with Knowledge Flow, I
always felt it was a bit limited and ended up just loading the
modelling dataset into Weka after it have been created elsewhere (ie
java/perl/python/sql/sas). One benefit of Weka is there a an amazing
number of learners implemented.

With Rattle there are some data preperation operations you can do
within the interface, but you can always fall back to the R prompt and
code it up if need be. Also if you build a model with Rattle you will
get the R code in the log which you can use to rebuild the model on a
regular basis (Weka can be invoked to build a model from the command
line but when you start chaining multiple operators & plugins together
it starts to get complicated). There may also be some financial
packages for R which may be of interest to you.

Tony: Impressive! Do you still do this sort of data mining? Thomas
A. Rathburn recently wrote a series of articles on data mining
financial markets which got me interested in this area. One of his
observations was that it is easier to predict direction rather than
specific price points, which makes sense. The articles are here:
http://www.b-eye-network.com/view/6386

Regards,
Shane
